subject: Unexpected 429s from tenant aliasing — remediation, evidence, and credit proposal
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Geller <matt@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected 429s from tenant aliasing — initial notice

Hi Matt,

Thanks for flagging the spike this morning. We see the 429s you reported for the /v1/generate endpoint between 08:40-08:55 PDT and are investigating. Early telemetry shows a subset of your requests were routed under an older tenant alias (cloudcrest-prod-v1) which still had a lower quota envelope attached. That mismatch caused enforcement at our ratecap layer even though your current plan should not have hit limits.

Immediate actions we're taking: 
- Route override: temporarily routing traffic from both aliases to your production quota while we correct the mapping (target: 30 minutes)
- Evidence capture: preserving request/response logs and enforcement traces (attached log snippet)
- Mitigation plan: a follow-up with concrete timeline and a proposed usage credit to reconcile customer impact

I'm copying Camila and Laura to coordinate credits and any contract implications. We will provide an updated timeline and full audit bundle by end of day.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll own the remediation and make sure you have what you need for your ops runbook.

Regards,
Nikhil
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quota-mapping-log-20280405.txt (log excerpt), recovery-checklist-steps.pdf (mitigation checklist)

From: Matt Geller <matt@cloudcrest.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@cloudcrest.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s from tenant aliasing — initial notice

Thanks Nikhil — appreciate the quick acknowledgement.

Impact: our customer-facing ingestion workers saw ~12% error rate for the 15m window; some queued jobs retried and caused downstream lag. Can you confirm whether any payloads were dropped (we're most concerned about lost events vs retryable 429s)?

Also need an ETA on the audit bundle and a preliminary credit estimate so I can brief our procurement team.

Matt
Head of Platform
CloudCrest

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s from tenant aliasing — mitigation update

Matt,

Quick update after the first round of triage:
- No payloads appear to be dropped at REDWOOD's ingestion layer — requests that received 429s were rejected by the ratecap enforcement and are retryable on your side. We will include a sample of request IDs in the audit bundle so you can correlate retries.
- Root cause: a stale tenant alias (cloudcrest-prod-v1) was inadvertently left behind during a plan migration two weeks ago. That alias kept an old quota constraint that our enforcement engine still honored because a namespace mapping failed to refresh.
- Fix applied: we pushed a mapping reconciliation which unlinked the stale alias and propagated the corrected quota envelope at 09:48 PDT. Post-fix telemetry shows error rate dropped to baseline within six minutes.

Next deliverables (EOD):
1) Full audit bundle (request IDs, enforcement traces, timestamped config snapshots)
2) Recovery checklist and suggested runbook updates for your on-call team (attached)
3) Proposed customer credit: 12% of the affected window usage billed to your account (detailed calc in attached spreadsheet)

Camila will follow up on the credit path and Laura will coordinate the postmortem. Evelyn — we may need the low-level kernel of the enforcement decision for the audit pack.

We'll also add an automatic alias-refresh job to reduce the chance of repeat mis-mappings; I'll include the proposed schedule in the audit bundle.

Best,
Nikhil

If you'd prefer a billable credit note or a waived invoice line, we can route through procurement — please let me know which you prefer.

Timing: we can issue the credit within 3 business days of sign-off.

Also including a link to the HubSpot ticket for your procurement team: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/CC-5482

Thanks for working through this; our ops and SRE teams will deliver the audit bundle by EOD and the postmortem summary within 72 hours.
